sources.kind: Manufacturer manual; illustrations generic within the 40175/640175 family
Manufacturer ring-spanner dimensions; generic tool candidate, not WABCO approval

pad_sequence.action: Obtain wheel access and isolate the brake; the published road-vehicle procedure removes a wheel. Railway wheel removal/access requires its own method.
With chamber retained, remove wear wiring if fitted, the lining-retainer screw and retainer, and three hold-down springs.
Open adjuster access, retract adjustment with the specified ring-spanner method, and support the pressure plate against rotation.
Shift caliper toward the wheel side to extract the outer pad; shift it toward the cylinder to extract the inner pad and pressure plate.

pad_installation_holds: Exact pad, retainer, three springs and pressure-plate solids are absent.
Adjuster and retainer tool axes/coordinates and service strokes have no controlled datum in this model.
Caliper is an extruded GA projection, not an OEM solid with service openings.
No accepted railway wheel-in-place pad-removal or lifting route is established.

candidate_tools.geometry_scope: Conservative full-length32OD external envelope, not complete socket solid. Internal engagement, torque-wrench head/extension/hand reach remain unverified.
candidate_tools.placement_scenario: C54 current illustrative nuts occupy s=-32 to-19; candidate envelope is s=-61 to-19 on each stud axis, plus straight extraction samples. Actual nut seat can change.

candidate_tools.geometry_scope: Catalog dimensions can inform a tool envelope, but no installed placement or WABCO equivalence is accepted.

installation_notes: Chamber removal views disconnect both hoses before translating the chamber; do not stretch connected hose models with chamber removal.
43mm stud length is a geometric lower bound against an ideal mounting plane, not complete removal clearance.
TRISTOP service hint prohibits washers, reinforcement plates and other securing devices at the chamber mounting; use specified new nuts and exact manufacturer installation data.
No pressure, service/parking-force, rotor fit, fatigue or operating acceptance is closed by service planning.
